audit.whatIsWrong: Four separate strings tell the player Rebuttal reflects Pop Blossom: wants.you[1] 'eat and reflect her E root and R stun projectiles', spikes[2].text 'W eats her clone-followup E and R projectiles, firing them back', whys[5] 'W shuts off her E-root and R-stun engage', and late 'your W keeps eating her R'.
audit.why: Pop Blossom is described by Riot as a leap that knocks up nearby enemies and stuns on landing — it is a point-blank AOE, not a projectile, and the kit flags it dash + hardCC with no projectile flag. Rebuttal reflects projectiles and prevents damage; there is nothing to reflect and nothing in its description stops crowd control. A Mel who holds W for the ult eats the stun anyway, which is exactly the death this matchup is supposed to prevent.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal can blank Pop Blossom's damage but cannot return it and does not stop the stun — answer it with distance.
sources: champ-data/_kits/neeko.json R Pop Blossom (dash + hardCC, no projectile flag)

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer mentions that immobilising crowd control breaks Inherent Glamour.
audit.why: Riot's own passive text: 'Receiving immobilizing crowd control, casting damaging spells, damaging enemy towers as a non-champion, or your disguise taking damage equal to its healthbar breaks the disguise.' Mel has a root on an 11s cooldown, so she is one of the cheapest disguise-checkers in the game — a Solar Snare on a suspicious 'ally' unmasks her instantly. That is real high-elo tech and it was absent.
audit.corrected: Added to phases[1].why and the content late text.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing mentions that Tangle-Barbs upgrades when it kills a unit.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'If the tangle kills an enemy or passes through a champion, it becomes larger, faster, and roots for longer.' This inverts the normal advice to hide behind minions — sheltering behind a low-HP minion is the single worst place to stand against her E, because the kill upgrades the projectile that is about to hit you.
audit.corrected: Added to phases[3].why and the content early text.

audit.whatIsWrong: The 'who roots first' framing in the content early text had no numbers behind it.
audit.why: Solar Snare is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9, Tangle-Barbs is 12/11.5/11/10.5/10. Mel's root is up first at every single rank. That is the mechanical reason the lane is winnable and it belongs in the text that claims it.
audit.corrected: Stated the 11s vs 12s comparison in breakdown.cooldowns, phases[1].why, whys[5] and the early text.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer calls this EVEN, 5.5/10, with every phase from level 2 onward marked 'Skill'. The content layer's chart gives Mel levels 2 through first item and the matchup sits at 60%.
audit.why: Both layers should agree, and here the content layer matches the win rate while the full layer does not.
audit.corrected: 4.5/10 with phases Skill / Mel x5 / Skill.
sources: scratchpad packet mel.json entry neeko (winRate 60, games 5, levelChart)

audit.whatIsWrong: The content late text says 'never facecheck for her invisible clone near objectives'.
audit.why: Shapesplitter's clone is a visible decoy that runs in a chosen direction and can be redirected — the whole point is that it looks like her. The kit description carries no invisibility on the clone. The thing that is genuinely hidden is Pop Blossom's wind-up while she is disguised, which is the fact worth warning about.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the disguised-ult warning and the Inherent Glamour break.
sources: champ-data/_kits/neeko.json W Shapesplitter and R Pop Blossom descriptions

edits.before: Even matchup — difficulty 5.5/10, Neeko carry threat 6/10.
edits.after: Favoured matchup — difficulty 4.5/10, Neeko carry threat 6/10.

edits.before: - Neeko Tangle-Barbs (Root): matchup-defining — The root sets up her whole burst — sidestep it behind minions. It governs your forward steps. - W Rebuttal spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Neeko Tangle-Barbs: 12s at rank 1 against your 11s Solar Snare — your root returns first at every rank, so you always get to open the trade. - Pop Blossom: 120s at rank 1, and its wind-up is hidden while she is wearing an ally's face.

edits.before: W Rebuttal online — the reflect turns his poke into your poke. Hold it for his real spell, not for chip.
edits.after: Solar Snare is 11s to her 12s Tangle-Barbs, and any immobilise breaks Inherent Glamour — your root unmasks her.

edits.before: Stack Overwhelm with every hit — once he's marked deep, your execute math starts working. Track Tangle-Barbs (Root) before stepping up.
edits.after: Tangle-Barbs comes out larger, faster and roots for longer once it has killed a unit — never shelter behind a dying minion.

edits.before: Golden Eclipse online — anyone you've stacked is now walking around with a countdown. Chip, stack, execute.
edits.after: Pop Blossom is a leap, not a projectile — Rebuttal blanks the damage but returns nothing, and the stun still lands.

edits.before: Hold W to eat and reflect her E root and R stun projectiles, denying her pick setup
edits.after: Hold W for Tangle-Barbs — Pop Blossom is a leap, not a projectile, nothing to reflect

edits.before: With mana and AP you chain Q pokes and W eats her clone-followup E and R projectiles, firing them back as your own damage — your peak.
edits.after: With mana and AP you chain Q pokes and Rebuttal answers Tangle-Barbs; Pop Blossom it can only blank, never return — your peak.

edits.before: Mana and AP let you chain Q pokes freely while W shuts off her E-root and R-stun engage — your most dominant window.
edits.after: Mana and AP let you chain Q pokes freely while Rebuttal answers Tangle-Barbs and your 11s root beats her 12s — your peak.

edits.before: Neeko is a fellow squishy mage with no escape, so the lane is about who lands their root first — and yours is better. At level 1 you both just trade autos and a single ability, roughly even. From level 2 your Q barrage plus Solar Snare's ~1.5s root means the moment she steps up to last-hit or winds up her own E, you root her and unload Q for free, and she has no dash to leave. Dodge her E (it telegraphs a thrown root) and hold W — if you time the barrier it eats her E projectile and fires it back as your damage.
edits.after: Neeko is a fellow squishy mage with no escape, so the lane is about who lands their root first — and yours is faster: Solar Snare is 11s against her 12s Tangle-Barbs at rank 1. At level 1 you both just trade autos and a single ability, roughly even. From level 2 the moment she steps up to last-hit or winds up her own E, you root her and unload Q for free. Watch what Tangle-Barbs passes through: if it kills a unit on the way it comes out larger, faster and roots for longer, so never shelter behind a dying minion.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are your takeover. Your Q ranks up, Overwhelm stacks pile from repeated pokes, and at 6 Golden Eclipse detonates all of it from any range — on a squishy Neeko that's an execute window. Bait her cooldowns: she'll feint with her W clone to disguise an engage, so don't burn your W or E on the fake. Her real threat is W-into-R: a clone repositions her, then her R AOE stun roots your dashless frame for a jungle collapse. Stay at max range, keep W up for her R, and she can't open on you.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are your takeover. Your Q ranks up, Overwhelm stacks pile from repeated pokes, and at 6 Golden Eclipse detonates all of it from any range — on a squishy Neeko that's an execute window. Bait her cooldowns: she'll feint with her W clone to disguise an engage, so don't burn your W or E on the fake. Her real threat is W-into-Pop Blossom. Rebuttal blanks that damage but cannot return it and will not stop the stun, so answer it with distance, not with a button.

edits.before: You stay even-to-favored straight up — she's as fragile as you, dies if your R catches her chunked, and your W keeps eating her R. The danger is never the 1v1: it's her R stun landing in a teamfight to set up a pick on your flashless, peel-less frame. Hold W for her engage, never facecheck for her invisible clone near objectives, and let your Overwhelm execute punish her the instant she's poked low. Win or end before she finds a five-man R off a clone flank.
edits.after: You stay even-to-favored straight up — she's as fragile as you, dies if your R catches her chunked, and your root arrives first. The danger is never the 1v1: it's Pop Blossom landing in a teamfight to set up a pick on your flashless, peel-less frame, and while she's disguised its wind-up is hidden entirely. Any immobilise breaks Inherent Glamour, so a Solar Snare on a suspicious ally unmasks her. Win or end before she finds a five-man R off a flank.

notes: FALSE POSITIVE: "Solar Snare's" flagged in spikes[0].text is correct — it is Mel's E. OUT-OF-BAND EDITS: full:diff ('EVEN' -> 'FAVOURED', 4 vs 8 chars) and full:phases[0..5].side. I left carryRating at 6/10 deliberately: Neeko's teamfight Pop Blossom is a genuine game-swinging threat even in a lane Mel wins, so lowering it would be wrong. SAMPLE SIZE: 5 games — I did not touch the 60% figure and the diffRating change to 4.5/10 is a modest move, not a rewrite, because the kit reasons for Mel's edge (11s vs 12s root, both squishy, no gap-closer on either side) are stronger evidence than five games are.
